source.name: Flame in Freefall official challenge statement

topicMatch.rationale: Material flammability is a core prevention measure for spacecraft crew environments.
topicMatch.sourceQuote: Prevention is achieved by controlling ignition sources and through material selection, which depends on understanding flammability limits.

solidFuelFlammability.rationale: The challenge identifies solid-material flammability studies as relevant to spacecraft fire safety.
solidFuelFlammability.sourceQuote: Flammability studies focus on solid materials such as fabrics and plastics

nasaFireSafetyLabel.rationale: PSI's normalized fire-safety sub-area labels are a direct catalog signal of relevance.
nasaFireSafetyLabel.sourceQuote: NASA's spacecraft fire safety work is focused on prevention, detection, and suppression.

microgravityProjectType.rationale: The challenge concerns low-gravity combustion investigations.
microgravityProjectType.sourceQuote: Results from low-gravity combustion experiments, conducted for example on the International Space Station (ISS)

topicMatch.rationale: Material flammability is especially relevant in the planned higher-oxygen, lower-pressure lunar environment.
topicMatch.sourceQuote: To facilitate spacesuit use, an atmosphere with increased oxygen and reduced pressure compared to Earth's is expected within the planned Moon Base and pressurized rovers.

solidFuelFlammability.rationale: The statement connects lunar habitat safety to flammability of solid materials.
solidFuelFlammability.sourceQuote: Flammability studies focus on solid materials such as fabrics and plastics

nasaFireSafetyLabel.rationale: PSI's normalized fire-safety sub-area labels are a direct catalog signal of relevance.
nasaFireSafetyLabel.sourceQuote: NASA's spacecraft fire safety work is focused on prevention, detection, and suppression.

moonBaseAtmosphere.rationale: This rewards investigations with measured tests in the challenge's expected lunar atmosphere zone; absence of test rows is not evidence against relevance.
moonBaseAtmosphere.sourceQuote: The intermediate oxygen concentration used on the Moon will likely be 30% or greater, with a corresponding pressure of 10.2 psi or less.

microgravityProjectType.rationale: The challenge concerns low-gravity combustion investigations.
microgravityProjectType.sourceQuote: Results from low-gravity combustion experiments, conducted for example on the International Space Station (ISS)

topicMatch.rationale: Smoke and aerosol measurement experiments are the challenge's named microgravity fire-detection work.
topicMatch.sourceQuote: Fire detection was tested in microgravity through the Smoke and Aerosol Measurement Experiment studies (SAME and SAME-R).

solidFuelFlammability.rationale: Solid samples and aerosols connect combustion investigations to smoke and particle detection.
solidFuelFlammability.sourceQuote: One of the instruments used for smoke detection in the SAME and SAME-R studies was instead used to detect dust in the Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test (DAFT and DAFT-2) studies.

nasaFireSafetyLabel.rationale: PSI's normalized fire-safety sub-area labels are a direct catalog signal of relevance.
nasaFireSafetyLabel.sourceQuote: NASA's spacecraft fire safety work is focused on prevention, detection, and suppression.

microgravityProjectType.rationale: The challenge names fire detection work conducted in microgravity.
microgravityProjectType.sourceQuote: Fire detection was tested in microgravity through the Smoke and Aerosol Measurement Experiment studies (SAME and SAME-R).

topicMatch.rationale: The challenge names FLEX as its microgravity fire-suppression investigation.
topicMatch.sourceQuote: Suppression was studied in the Flame Extinguishment Experiment (FLEX) through dilution of the chamber atmosphere with carbon dioxide and helium, both of which suppress fire.

solidFuelFlammability.rationale: The suppression profile focuses on suppressant effectiveness rather than fuel phase.
solidFuelFlammability.sourceQuote: Suppression was studied in the Flame Extinguishment Experiment (FLEX) through dilution of the chamber atmosphere with carbon dioxide and helium, both of which suppress fire.

nasaFireSafetyLabel.rationale: PSI's normalized fire-safety sub-area labels are a direct catalog signal of relevance.
nasaFireSafetyLabel.sourceQuote: NASA's spacecraft fire safety work is focused on prevention, detection, and suppression.

microgravityProjectType.rationale: The challenge names suppression work conducted in microgravity.
microgravityProjectType.sourceQuote: Suppression was studied in the Flame Extinguishment Experiment (FLEX) through dilution of the chamber atmosphere with carbon dioxide and helium, both of which suppress fire.
